You just need to care about whether Tim Moore keeps fighting for you in Congress. [](https://timmoore.cmail20.com/t/y-l-fwftl-hkhielhuy-r/) **Friday, July 31st | 5:00 PM | Gaston Country Club, 3700 County Club Drive, Gastonia, NC** I'll be there. Tim will be there. The only thing missing is you. This event is part of that. Friend, July 31st is coming in just a few days, and with it our end-of-month fundraising deadline. _Before we ask you to chip in, can we take a minute to explain why this deadline matters so much?_ This deadline is about more than just a number. What we raise before August will help determine how strong our campaign is heading into November, and how much we can invest in organizing, reaching voters, supporting Democrats up and down the ballot, and responding to Republican attacks. Martin is taking on some of the biggest fights facing New Mexicans and our country. He voted against a defense bill that would give the Trump administration a blank check for a reckless war with Iran. He’s fighting attempts to sell off treasured public lands like the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge for oil and gas drilling. And he’s standing up to the decisions driving up grocery, housing, health care, and energy costs for working families. **But Martin cannot take on these fights alone.** Republicans and their wealthy allies are already pouring money into races across the country. | | | Dear Friend, **Across Alaska, elections are conducted, public records maintained, and local governments kept running by dedicated local government clerks. Yet many communities are struggling to fill these essential positions**. We're writing today with an exciting update: Build Alaska's Future has launched the first of three new short-form videos for our [Clerks initiative](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136252647/636837356/-656634486?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzEwMjc1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhZGNkMDNlNC1hOThiLWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=A5A6gjE0ZJNlyjev2IJvhCpYr-PU1ib94m8rhNfkFmo=&emci=ad860abd-9d86-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&emdi=adcd03e4-a98b-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&ceid=9512399), and we'd love your help spreading the word. [**'Good Work, Close to Home'**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/136252649/636837358/1504491898?si=tsqJ0FZULZcZ0qef&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzEwMjc1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhZGNkMDNlNC1hOThiLWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=A5A6gjE0ZJNlyjev2IJvhCpYr-PU1ib94m8rhNfkFmo=&emci=ad860abd-9d86-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&emdi=adcd03e4-a98b-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&ceid=9512399) **This first video is a call to action for Alaskans looking for stable, meaningful work close to home**. It features Donald Jones of Kotzebue, Beth McEwen of Juneau, and Gina Gregg of Fairbanks, who share their own experiences as clerks and why the work matters. **Local government clerks are the backbone of civic life:** they run elections, maintain public records, and keep town, city, and tribal offices functioning. name: Abdul El-Sayed
subject: Can’t stop thinking about this…
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Abdul for U
body:
Hi Peter,
I know it's late, but my mind is swirling thinking about these AIPAC ads.
AIPAC-aligned super PACs have now dumped $59+ million into Michigan to prop up their preferred candidate. It’s hard to even picture what that much money could do.
**But despite that unfathomable amount of cash, I still think we’re going to win next Tuesday.** Here’s why:
AIPAC has done this before, in primary races just like ours. It's spent millions trying to bury campaigns that wouldn't play by its rules — and in almost every one of those races, one of two scenarios plays out:
1. When a campaign has the resources to tell its own story and break through the noise, AIPAC's ads don't land.
2. When a campaign runs dry, gets overwhelmed, and can't respond, that's when AIPAC's ads seal their fate.

So the honest answer to whether we get through this isn't complicated. It comes down to whether we have enough grassroots power to keep running our own ads, reaching our own voters, and maintain control of our story before AIPAC defines it for us.

subject: Less than 100 days to go
body:
With less than 100 days left, it is time to go all in.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
**We’re LESS THAN 100 days away from Election Day. To mark 100 days out we activated hundreds of volunteers**** _in over 50 countie_****s this weekend alone.**
We just want to say _thank you_ to everyone who came out, and we’d like to take a moment to tell you how everyone fighting to get Gina Hinojosa elected to be the next Governor of Texas spent this past weekend. This matters because...
Before the election is called...
Before ballots are cast...

What can we take away from all this court news? That opponents of voting rights aren't going to stop attacking vote-by-mail. They're not deterred by losing one Supreme Court case, and they'll appeal every other decision all the way there as well, if they need to. The legal costs don't matter to them, since the voter suppression movement is well-funded by a few billionaires.
Our grassroots movement is fighting back, but our work is only possible with your help. Pitch in $35 or more right now to defend vote-by-mail and make every vote count in our elections >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=072826_2&amount=35]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
DemocracyDocket: Appeals court backs Trump bid to block some mail ballots, for now, as Supreme Court mulls issue [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=072826_2&amount=35]
Bad news today, Team.
A federal appeals court ruled today that the Trump administration may continue implementing President Donald Trump’s anti-mail voting executive order . The U.S. Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia affirmed a lower court’s decision, holding that a lawsuit challenging the constitutionality of Trump’s March 2026 edict was premature because the administration hasn’t executed it yet.
This is a different case from the U.S. Supreme Court's recent ruling on counting mail-in ballots received after Election Day . That case, Watson V. RNC , ended with rational minds choosing to count ballots that were mailed on time.
This case is different: Trump's Executive Order from March 2026 ordered the U.S. Postal Service (USPS) to send mail ballots in new barcoded envelopes only to voters on citizenship lists compiled by the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and the Social Security Administration. After defenders of voting rights quickly sued, a U.S. District Court Judge denied the preliminary injunction back in May, saying it would be premature to issue it when the federal agencies hadn’t begun implementation yet. The appeal of that ruling is what was decided today.
It's worth noting that both courts said the case was "premature," which means that no voter had yet been harmed by the order, so the court was unable to rule on the merits of the case. This means that neither court made any decision on the merits of the case brought to protect mail-in ballots.
Listen, we know this is a lot of information, Team. The long and short of it is that we need your help to keep standing up to this Executive Order and protect mail-in voting. The Executive Order to have USPS work with DHS and Social Security to subvert the Constitution purports to address “non-citizen voting.” States, however, already have proven systems in place to verify voter eligibility, non-citizen voting is already a federal crime, and instances are vanishingly rare.
Of course, this ruling came just a day after the DOJ asked the U.S. Supreme Court to lift a block on implementing the order in 23 Democratic-led states and Washington, D.C. upheld just a few days ago, in a separate case ( California V. Trump ).
It's simple: These Trump executive orders are dangerous, unlawful, and harmful to voters. We will never stay silent when the right to vote is attacked, Team, including by a hostile administration in control of the federal government.

clean_body: And the results speak for themselves: more violence, divorce, abortion, drug addiction, depression, and the breakdown of the family. | | | | Dear Friend, Will you help me put God back in your town schools? | | | They are wonderfully made in the very image of God. And that God is calling them to love Him above all else. What a country we'd be, if all of America's children had just a little bit of God's Word in their lives - like you did. Our Founding Fathers understood this. That's why throughout our history, the Bible has been the cornerstone of American life, education, and law. Abraham Lincoln believed the Bible was "the best gift God has given to man." And Dwight D. Eisenhower said, "Without God there could be no American form of government, nor an American way of life." But in 1963, in a wrongly decided Supreme Court case, the Left ripped the everyday reading of the Bible out of public schools. And the results speak for themselves: more violence, divorce, abortion, drug addiction, depression, and the breakdown of the family. Justice Stewart Potter was the lone dissenter in the Supreme Court decision that outlawed the mandatory reading of the Bible in schools. He wrote that the ruling didn't 'protect religious freedom' but rather 'established a religion of secularism.' And how right he was! But even Justice Potter wouldn't have predicted how far the 'religion of secularism' has taken us from Biblical values. ...today radical "educators" teach our children and grandchildren that: God is a myth for the weak and if their families believe in Him, they're probably uneducated, hateful, and racist. If these "educators" do acknowledge God, they say He makes mistakes and some boys are really girls and some girls are really boys. And they wrongly tell children, 'God just wants you to be happy' so you should do whatever you want, do whatever feels good, and anyone who tells you otherwise is an old- fashioned bigot who has to go. So many families are being torn apart by this madness that overturns everything our Founders believed. It is only fitting that during the 250th Anniversary of our independence, we put Biblical lessons BACK into our public schools. Your signature on your "Schools Need a Bible Revival" petition tells our elected officials that you want biblical lessons put back in our public schools. Think public schools are too far gone? Think I'm dreaming? Consider this... BRAVE FOR GOOD is the powerhouse group behind my "See You at the Library" movement featured on Fox News, that gets conservative Story Hours into public libraries to counter the Left's "Drag Queen Story Hours." BRAVE FOR GOOD is the powerhouse group that got an historic conservative Story Hour into the Library of Congress last year! And BRAVE FOR GOOD is the powerhouse group that will get the Biblical values you cherish - and that America was founded upon - back into public schools this year! HOW? We've designed a mini-curriculum for America's 250th Anniversary that teaches children about the role of the Bible in our nation's Founding and emphasizes the Founding values that have made our country great. Last year I got into three public schools to reach 1,400 children with biblical lessons. With you and BRAVE FOR GOOD behind me, I know we can expand that number to 250,000 children this year in honor of America's 250th Anniversary. You know it won't be easy. The radical leftists who've taken over our public schools aren't just going to put out the welcome mat. That's why BRAVE FOR GOOD is getting ready for the battle by collecting stacks of petitions. Your signed petition tells our representatives that the Supreme Court ruling that took the Bible out of schools only specified that the Bible could not be mandatory reading. The 1963 ruling 100% allows for the Bible to be taught in a historical or cultural context! And why wouldn't it be? In every corner of the world, the Bible is considered one of the greatest books ever written. Of course children should learn about it in your taxpayer-funded schools! But radical educators will try to keep anything to do with the Bible out of our schools and when they do, BRAVE FOR GOOD will be ready to counter them with thousands of signed petitions. And will you please also consider a tax-deductible petition sponsorship gift of $35 or more? Every petition you send digitally must still be delivered, verified, securely collected, and tabulated before it can be presented -- That means your gift today puts hundreds of new voices on the record before the deadline. To be blunt, BRAVE FOR GOOD is a small but mighty Christian non-profit and this Bible Revival is funded entirely as a grassroots effort from patriots like you. It won't be easy going up against taxpayer-funded public schools and their unlimited money. But I know we can do it. Together with BRAVE FOR GOOD and patriots like you , we got conservative and patriotic values back into public libraries. Only God can lead our nation back to His Word. Thank you for standing with us. Sincerely, | | | Kirk Cameron BRAVE For Good | | | | ** Our best chance to put the biblical values our nation was founded upon back into schools is this year during America's 250th Anniversary so please hurry. | | | BRAVE FOR GOOD is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization. * 61% ages 30–44.
* 46% of men.
* 46% of women.
* And more than 40% in every region of Wisconsin.

We talk a lot about the broad, diverse coalition we’re building, and it's showing up in the Marquette poll.

body:
| |

Hi Peter,

Campaigns generate a lot of noise. I want to tell you what I have actually delivered.

I wrote SB 35, which has **accelerated thousands of homes across California, including over 4,000 affordable homes in San Francisco.**

I wrote SB 79, which **made it legal to build more housing near major public transit**. People said it could not pass. We built a coalition, took on entrenched opposition, and got it signed into law.

When **BART and Muni faced financial collapse, I helped secure $1.1 billion in emergency state funding and another $500 million loan**. Then I passed legislation allowing the Bay Area to **create a permanent source of transit funding**.

I wrote the law **capping insulin at $35 a month** and it took effect this January.

I wrote the nation's **first law requiring billion-dollar corporations to disclose their carbon emissions**. The oil and gas lobby fought it for years. California is implementing it right now, while the Trump administration dismantles federal climate rules.

I wrote the **nation’s first law prohibiting ICE and other law enforcement officers from hiding behind masks**. When Trump’s Department of Homeland Security demanded a veto, we stood firm and got it signed.

I wrote the **No Kings Act to give people a path to justice when federal agents violate their constitutional rights**. It passed the California Senate 30 to 10.

I also wrote **California’s transgender refuge law, which protects families fleeing states that criminalize gender-affirming care** and inspired similar protections across the country.

That is the kind of leadership I will bring to Congress.

Identify a hard problem. Build a coalition. Take the heat. Get something done.

We close the books on July tomorrow night. clean_body: | | Hi Peter, Campaigns generate a lot of noise. I want to tell you what I have actually delivered. I wrote SB 35, which has accelerated thousands of homes across California, including over 4,000 affordable homes in San Francisco. I wrote SB 79, which made it legal to build more housing near major public transit. People said it could not pass. We built a coalition, took on entrenched opposition, and got it signed into law. When BART and Muni faced financial collapse, I helped secure $1.1 billion in emergency state funding and another $500 million loan. Then I passed legislation allowing the Bay Area to create a permanent source of transit funding. I wrote the law capping insulin at $35 a month and it took effect this January. I wrote the nation's first law requiring billion-dollar corporations to disclose their carbon emissions. The oil and gas lobby fought it for years. California is implementing it right now, while the Trump administration dismantles federal climate rules. I wrote the nation’s first law prohibiting ICE and other law enforcement officers from hiding behind masks. When Trump’s Department of Homeland Security demanded a veto, we stood firm and got it signed. I wrote the No Kings Act to give people a path to justice when federal agents violate their constitutional rights. It passed the California Senate 30 to 10. I also wrote California’s transgender refuge law, which protects families fleeing states that criminalize gender-affirming care and inspired similar protections across the country. That is the kind of leadership I will bring to Congress. Identify a hard problem. Build a coalition. Take the heat. Get something done. ---|---|---
A formerly illicit Chinese cannabis grow was the site of an armed robbery on Wednesday, but the Kennebec Sheriff's Office is releasing few details on who robbed the pot growers and whether the burglary was related to the Asian Transnational Criminal Organizations that have infested Maine with clandestine cannabis cultivation sites.
A source who asked not to be named identified the property as 211 Bartlett Road in Belgrade, one of at least nine locations in Belgrade that federal or state law enforcement suspects of operating as an illicit marijuana grow.
The last time Chinese organized crime saw a law enforcement action in Belgrade was in [January 2024](https://substack.com/redirect/d2c0a25c-1468-446d-98a3-f824159ccaed?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), when two related drug operations on Point Road and Guptill Road were taken down on the same day. Those operations led to the arrest of 66-year-old Lin Min Chan of Florida and 44-year-old Yuequan Chen, as well as the confiscation of 2,300 live marijuana plants. The Guptill Road property was owned by Ying Ci Mei, 50, of Brooklyn, N.Y., while the Point Road property was owned by Siu Yin Huang, 65, of Uncasville, Conn.
Sheriff's deputies said three men entered a residential building in Belgrade, tied up two individuals, and then stole all the marijuana and an undisclosed amount of money. One of the suspects pointed a gun at the victims while they were being tied up, WGME reported. The Kennebec Sheriff's Office did not release any information about the couple living at the home at the time of the burglary or the potential suspects.
According to real estate records, tax records, corporate records, and electrical records, the property is controlled by Yiqiang Huang, a Mandarin-speaking cannabis entrepreneur who is well known to regulators at the Office of Cannabis Policy.
Huang purchased the property in Sept. 2023. Like more than 75 other Chinese cannabis growers, he financed the property using a loan from [Quontic Bank](https://substack.com/redirect/f4f2a17e-c9e4-43ca-a3af-ca07feda4c01?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), a bank in New York that has made a fortune offering special loans to foreign nationals and non-citizens -- loans that are de-risked by the taxpayer-funded Community Development Financial Institution (CDFI) designation.
RELATED:
* [Treasury Drops Hammer on ex-Quontic Bank Mortgager Linked to Maine's Chinese Cannabis Houses](https://substack.com/redirect/7e0ffed8-b399-4b3a-8251-d143f1e89016?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* [Triad Weed: One NYC Bank Financed More Than 50 Illicit Chinese Marijuana Grow Houses in Rural Maine](https://substack.com/redirect/4bccc3c3-0680-447b-adfd-0b3439944eca?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* [How the U.S. Treasury Department Helps Chinese Organized Crime Transform American Homes Into Drug Dens](https://substack.com/redirect/f4f2a17e-c9e4-43ca-a3af-ca07feda4c01?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

Immediately after closing on the property, Huang installed 400-amp commercial grade electricity -- a physical prerequisite for converting a middle-class Maine home into a dingy marijuana dump. The electrical permit record explicitly states that the increased power was for a cannabis cultivation operation.
Huang began cultivating cannabis illegally right away, according to OCP records obtained by _The Robinson Report_ under a Freedom of Access Act request. Only later, in March 2024, did he attempt to apply for a medicinal cannabis registration from the state. But, as part of that process, the state caught Huang running an unlicensed grow, denied his caregiver application, and even said in writing that he'd falsified his paperwork.

The state never filed charges against him for falsifying his paperwork.

## US Resumes Strikes on Iran After Missile Attack

## Fauci Pleads the Fifth More than 100 Times
Dr. Anthony Fauci [invoked the Fifth Amendment](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0MEO2yAQBNCvwTciWEzsHDhUqqxe0muPFoZ1vA2GCDaJ_PdV8gs9jzR6M3-u89VTonz77Xd0vJY547slZMY6N650x1YyVZ8rtueOq38Gesyg4CzVII2ao6d0zH0X3YoIaDp0ehhtr87GQLc544dg-qgijBer9KqjHRVEuw5Ghz5AR-7TpgajtNKg1Wkxiw2Lsr324yVEK3qFkbjU099CmTdc01FeWE-h7F1yG_OjCfNDwCRg8kv4LPhkAqZf6BNvAqavW1J-lTs2aXmTfsccd8wsG2bPKBkb017yISuu1VNu0uf2xkr5JmBqXOohzERRmJ_aWD1aMLarLj7elBK18yB6dds9pS-M_-vNl4N_AQAA__-42Yog) at a Senate hearing Wednesday, refusing to answer questions about the COVID-19 pandemic. It was the first time the 85-year-old had done so in more than 250 appearances before Congress. Fauci [pleaded the Fifth more than 100 times](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDHO4yAUhE-DOyIMGDsFxTbusu2WFjaP8HYxWPCSyLdfOVf4u5FG-jTf_HksD4cJ8_O328FSKEuGT0tABHVpVPEftJKxulyhvXYI7rXhsUghDRcjV2LxDtO56M7bACBBdWD7cRq0MErJLtrNu6DuYt3CJMJkBr2uxgyrNmby0Pe6Q3vRxKhEL3rZi9uq1mFbxaB7N903PzAtwCOVevtbMFOEkM7yhnrbyt4lG4mOxtQvJmcm53wepdFVMTlfYCZnMV75zuT8avzyY3J2mWLJJ_8K8SOB841TBB4wUORuh-x3yMQx8wbZEfAIrmJ-Mjl31frjgylhMyPT4rk7TN859KMP31b-DwAA___RW4Xs) over three hours, and his attorney was ejected from the room. Former President Biden preemptively pardoned Fauci, but Republicans argue [any new false statements](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLHSpCAQhJ8GM6wBRN2A4BKzvfRCC2Vc5w6BAlxr3_7KfYU_m6rp6v66_zznpyVP4fXbHmjqFueAV_FYK-a51Ez_sMRA2YaM5Txws-dKaZYgew4DVzA7S_4zd40zG6JE1aARw6g76JWSzW40Dg76BdYRxba48aHVKPpeurETMAjbkLndYFAgQEgB7aIWvS6gO2HHx-o06wAd1Zjbv5FC3XHzn_jG3K7xaLzZa02FqV9MTkxO13W1KXqqtMZbwOTk6Y38TM5WLExOdxqTEwz3_WByWmN4ZSz3L9vgeLKn59-ifCGHgSebXQx8o63u3B4Y3IGh8ptXCw1NNi5d5D2VfmAdvA5L_gtXf7To28j_AQAA__9xf4lT) would fall outside that protection and expose him to perjury charges. Paul announced the committee [will vote next week](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0D2u2zAQBODTSN0aFKkfq2CRRt1Lm1KgyKW1MX8Eci3l3T6wr_DqAQbzzZ-v9ctQoPT4bSJq9nlNeNWAzFjWyoWeWHOiYlLB-orozcvSsUohRxATKLE6Q-F77VunPaJE1aLupvvQi1Ep2e5aqM2P99FubrCi96Pv_OQcznMnt2mefUv63SYmJTrRyU7cNrUNdhND35n7bN3Q9AIdcS63v5kS7-jDdz6x3GyObdA781Eb9auRSyOX67puPv97K955I5cjB2KytZFLMcnBYV4BKuKzgqWTAticGOPBYHdTHljBeMYCHypQOvMTK3jyvIOJmFzExBBzQeDdJJgEMEWsbdHuuCgEquPU9OIRDYXPRv7RsaeW_wMAAP__FCuRhg) on referring Fauci for contempt of Congress. He questioned whether the Fifth Amendment even applies to someone holding a pardon.
## New Six Flags Coaster to Break 6 World Records
Six Flags Great Adventure unveiled [a record-breaking new roller coaster](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2uozAQRp8GOqPB_GULF9vQZdstkbHHZDbGjmacEPbpr3Jf4VZf8-no6Py9LldLkdL2x-5oSshLwkMiloK8SGG6o-REbBOjPHcM9unosWjQo4JJdbB4S_Fc-tqbgKixq9G002XoYew6Xd9MO7gJB-gvbnLgfQshaLfiuIJ2g7a-JvOhwdRBC61uoVm7dXArDH1rL7-cH6oe0FPJ3PzLlMoNQzzzC7lxea-juZXykKr7Xem50vNxHE3I7_UplFDk86n0HCmglDNipWehtwrRbqI4x4isXLZSkNXKaO9qVEfm6BWjy-xFFWSmcFLalN3t_88yeazZ-MdBMZKMU9XDtluK30blRxlfRn8FAAD__zqbi1w) Tuesday that will send riders 382 feet into the sky at 100 mph. Bakunawa, named for a moon-devouring sea serpent from Philippine mythology, opens at the New Jersey park in 2027. The ride will claim [six world records](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGOszAQBOCnMV3Qeo0DFC7-hi5_eyVamyXxxeDINrHy9ifuFa6bYvSNNF-3-UY--P3-nzY2ZY3zzjUHLoXTnEvyT85x94n2xPnYeKXD-deMgNcL9BcF80I-fOauWczKjKwaNrIfdAdXpbB5GKcJOqVHiQjW6tUCL6NjNUg5MvWy8ebUoFcgQaKE1iqrnQXdSRpGt2jRAS--xNR-R7-XB6_hE9-cWhe3JphHKa8s1D-Bk8Cp1tq6SLlwkiDPisDpHBA4QX_mQeBk6XnsVEng1CSzvKoPwedrLzq4b-TDL13-9Mfb4E8AAAD__8y9cb8), including the world's first upside-down launch. Riders will accelerate from 60 to 80 mph while fully inverted. Free-spinning, floorless trains rotate independently throughout the 3,163-foot course, [so no two rides are identical](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL3OozAQAJ8GOkfG5i-Fi2vocu2VaLHXsBdjI3sJl3v6T_le4etHo9H8ecwPoEBx_Q07GvZpjniVgMyY58KZnlhSpAwxYzl39HBaOmYlVS_kILScHVB4z23tjEdUqGs0zTB2rey1VvVm7GjHewsd2gXt3Tu9tI1CaYcOOtl7X5P52OSgZSMb1cjbopfOLrJrGxjv1nVVK9ERp3z7myjyhj680wvzzaa9DmZjPkqlf1VqqtQEzBksU4plhxX-U8QPV6mp0D_hA6xFrBmBBbgXRj4zigWeZ4QLhE1QGLM4j0IOhUtXFAHOaLdKTXU27rgoBCr9ULVy3YHCdwP_aNzLqK8AAAD__x6thls). Each trip lasts about two minutes and 17 seconds. Bakunawa rises near the former site of Kingda Ka, the beloved 456-foot giant demolished last year after two decades as an icon of the park. [See the concept footage here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2OqzAQxfGnMV3QMDYfKVxcKUqXW620SoWMGYfZGIxsEzZvv2JfYdtzpF_x_7z1N8Oel8d_M5POLvQL7clTzhT7lCM_KYWFo1kipW0mZzbLa4-AzQnak4R-NOzfvSpG7YiQZEG6artaQSMlFpPGzp5b05mzU4TOUNeAtBJrRxWOOKiC9aFBK6GCCisoBznUdoBaVaY727EWCmjkHGL5FXjJEzn_Di-KpQ1z4fWU85qE_CfwKvC673v5DlveBjr-YzHZTkJeX0Je8I7D9-W-Xj6eRdTjurP3nJpWKHjMhv0vmf_U4aXxJwAA__-RSnGh).

**Dear _Flyover_ Reader,** A month ago, the _Minnesota Star Tribune_ won a Pulitzer Prize. Last week, it announced it's cutting 15% of its staff.

That's been the shape of the whole year. In February, the _Washington Post_ eliminated more than 300 newsroom jobs and closed its sports and books desks outright. The BBC is shedding up to 2,000 roles. BuzzFeed and HuffPost cut about a third of their people. In Pittsburgh, the _Post-Gazette_ shuttered its entire opinion section and published its last editorial.

Here's what none of those outlets will say out loud: this is what happens when you spend years telling your audience what to think instead of what happened. Readers can tell when the news is tilted, and they've been walking away by the millions.

The numbers back it up. Gallup now finds just 28% of Americans trust the media to report the news fully, accurately, and fairly. That's the lowest it has ever measured.

The legacy media created this problem. _The Flyover_ was built to be the solution, and the difference is simple. They editorialize in their reporting. We don't. They tell you what to think about the news; we just show you what happened, clearly and fairly, and trust you to make up your own mind.

And it's working: while they shrink, we're about to cross six million readers. Six million Americans who start their morning with the facts and decide for themselves. They're fleeing the spin, and they're finding us.

_The Flyover_ will always be free. Producing it isn't.

So as we close in on six million, let me ask you two questions:

Do you rely on us for news without the spin? Is fact-first journalism worth fighting for?

If your answer is yes, will you chip in and help us hit this milestone at full speed?

I'll be honest with you: I read the same headlines you do, and there are mornings this industry looks like it's coming apart. Hey, Peter – Roy here. I just wanted to follow up on the new attack ads running against me.
With Senate control at stake here in North Carolina, the Senate GOP’s super PAC – the Senate Leadership Fund – launched their largest ad reservation in the country to attack me (nearly two months _earlier_ than they initially planned). Roy Cooper

## Cornyn Holds Up Blanche Confirmation
Republican Sen. John Cornyn said on Wednesday that he's "[not prepared to vote yes](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD2OgzAUhE9jOkf-A0PhYhu6bLsleuAHtmTsyLwl4far5Apbj2ZG3_dzn-4QU8zbN-zo6LWWKePzSEiEdZp_a0RfwccCC8UTdyCsEdKkhOq4sFyLyUNM12Qa72bhB9mgk7ZvjRh0Z5vgjLbWGKlF6xXYtm97OStAva5GLq2VTXTvMWG1kFIo091mLeSyCmG6xWotV2YE-kil3igg4QuONV3lxHpbyt4kF4geB9NfTI1MjRQwxJTeGVNjKDu-gZgaD8xAyNTYDkNnh54vpeYr8zlBXgLyHZFi3jgQlZrx4htmrJD4WT61pjr_eMaU4tFZZsS2Q_zcNPQ_cadTfwEAAP__3j6CLA)" on confirming attorney general nominee Todd Blanche, whose nomination can't clear the Senate Judiciary Committee without him. Cornyn [wants written proof](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD1u3DAQRk9DdVwMf0ytCxZp1DltSmEkDlcTUKRBTVar2wdOjuD-w4f33q-P-QO5cH38xJ2ivHKbK51HIRHq8_KnM6WOiRuuwk_aUagzltmCDRpG7WBOyOWa_ZDiAundDBTNeH_z8O7COGwx2ODvIRvw4W4dZAzkrAmAOd8hpDRw_DqD0YExYH24LQ7MmgF8WEfnTFYeKLG0fpONhF545HK1J_Xb2vahxE3k81Duh7KTstN5nrcTj43rQ1qlF-5c_0-Vnb7clJ0Oqiik7ORDGOENlJ2kpaSXgnXdSJe2LJf-3baq19brVTWKtF7p0g-q1LHotdXMfUfhVpWdhh7T58ml8BFG5eGxI5d_fPK9qs9o_wYAAP__6umNfg) that the Justice Department has formally killed a proposed $1.8 billion "anti-weaponization" fund, created in President Trump's IRS settlement to compensate people claiming political persecution, and a narrower version of the deal's tax-audit immunity for Trump. **Dear**** _Texas Flyover_****Reader,**
A month ago, the _Minnesota Star Tribune_ won a Pulitzer Prize. Last week, it announced it's cutting 15% of its staff.

That's been the shape of the whole year. In February, the _Washington Post_ eliminated more than 300 newsroom jobs and closed its sports and books desks outright. The BBC is shedding up to 2,000 roles. BuzzFeed and HuffPost cut about a third of their people. In Pittsburgh, the _Post-Gazette_ shuttered its entire opinion section and published its last editorial.

Here's what none of those outlets will say out loud: this is what happens when you spend years telling your audience what to think instead of what happened. Readers can tell when the news is tilted, and they've been walking away by the millions.

The numbers back it up. Gallup now finds just 28% of Americans trust the media to report the news fully, accurately, and fairly. That's the lowest it has ever measured.

The legacy media created this problem. _The Texas Flyover_ was built to be the solution, and the difference is simple. They editorialize in their reporting. We don't. And it's working: while they shrink, we're about to cross six million readers. Six million Americans who start their morning with the facts and decide for themselves. They're fleeing the spin, and they're finding us.

_The Texas Flyover_ will always be free. Producing it isn't.

In February, the Washington Post eliminated more than 300 newsroom jobs and closed its sports and books desks outright. The BBC is shedding up to 2,000 roles. BuzzFeed and HuffPost cut about a third of their people. In Pittsburgh, the Post-Gazette shuttered its entire opinion section and published its last editorial. Here's what none of those outlets will say out loud: this is what happens when you spend years telling your audience what to think instead of what happened. Readers can tell when the news is tilted, and they've been walking away by the millions. The numbers back it up. Gallup now finds just 28% of Americans trust the media to report the news fully, accurately, and fairly. That's the lowest it has ever measured. The legacy media created this problem. The Texas Flyover was built to be the solution, and the difference is simple. They editorialize in their reporting. We don't. They tell you what to think about the news; we just show you what happened, clearly and fairly, and trust you to make up your own mind. And it's working: while they shrink, we're about to cross six million readers. Six million Americans who start their morning with the facts and decide for themselves. They're fleeing the spin, and they're finding us. The Texas Flyover will always be free. Producing it isn't. So as The Flyover family of readers closes in on six million, let me ask you two questions: Do you rely on us for news without the spin? Is fact-first journalism worth fighting for? Fifty years ago, Alex Haley's Roots changed how this country understood its own history.

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/e3dabd02da88/stand-up-against-the-shameful-gop-power-grab-7363780?e=dc5f639d62)

Hey friends,
**I’m thrilled to share with you episode 3 of the** _**Standing Tall**_**podcast!**
_****_
**
CLICK HERE:**[**LISTEN NOW**](https://us.list-manage.com/c8WidoC60xS?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0)
Fifty years ago, Alex Haley's _Roots_ changed how this country understood its own history. This year, on the anniversary of that book, a Tennessee school district [banned it](https://us.list-manage.com/1B3DA6aUpJf?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0) from library shelves — in the same city that has a 13-foot statue of Haley holding that very book.
**This week I sat down with Chris Haley (Alex Haley's great-nephew) and Bill Haley Jr. (his grandson, and a 9th-generation descendant of Kunta Kinte himself)** to talk about all of it — the cultural impact _Roots_ had in 1976, the recent ban and its reversal here in Knox County, and what it means that we're fighting some of these same battles again today. We also get into the upcoming [Roots 50th Commemorative Experience](https://us.list-manage.com/gCthoczYYwS?e=dc5f639d62&c2id=395895520870fa96cf2587ee59cac4d0), a three-day immersive tour kicking off August 7th!
This one's personal, it's historical, and it's exactly the kind of conversation we needed to have right now.

| | **The Four-Day Pause Collapsed. Brent Settled at $90 After an 8% Daily Jump. The Oil Market Has Now Cycled Through Four Ceasefire Bounces. Here Is the Full Price Ledger of a War That Refuses to End.**
---
| | Oil steadied after the biggest daily jump in more than two weeks, as the US launched a fresh wave of strikes against targets in Iran. Brent traded near $90 a barrel after rallying by almost 8% in the previous session, while West Texas Intermediate was above $84. The oil market has now priced four ceasefire-collapse cycles in this war. April 8 ceasefire announcement: Brent –15.9%. Two days later: +8% reversal. June 17 MOU signing: Brent –$22 over a month. July 8 collapse: Brent +$10 in two days. July 25 pause: Brent –11.3% on Monday. July 29 collapse: Brent +8% same session. Each cycle compresses: the market learns faster that the ceasefire is fragile, prices the fragility sooner, and the initial decline gets shallower while the recovery gets faster. The four-day pause produced the smallest ceasefire-premium deflation and the fastest reversal of any ceasefire event in the war. The market is running out of surprise. What it retains is structural: Hormuz at fewer than 10 ships per day, Bab-el-Mandeb down 22%, Kazakhstan CPC still suspended — these are not price movements. They are physical supply absences that persist regardless of diplomatic announcements.
---
| | Petroleum markets in the second quarter of 2026 were characterized by continued disruptions to international crude oil and petroleum product flows through the Strait of Hormuz, contributing to higher and more volatile crude oil prices through most of the quarter. Crude oil inventories held at storage facilities in Cushing, Oklahoma, fell below 20 million barrels during the week ending June 19 until the week ending July 10. Cushing below 20 million barrels is operationally significant — at that level, pipeline minimums and tank bottom constraints begin to affect physical delivery. The July recovery briefly brought Cushing back above 20 million. The resumed war is drawing it down again. The August 11 STEO, now 12 days away, must model both the resumed war's demand on physical storage and the structural damage to Gulf supply routes that no ceasefire announcement can quickly repair.
---
